metadata.teaching_provenance: RCET3373-planning F26 W04D01 Timer0 teaching record

questions.stem: A PIC16F883 uses a 4 MHz oscillator and Timer0 uses the internal instruction clock with no prescaler. What is the Timer0 increment period?

feedback.correct: Correct. With the internal source, Timer0 uses the instruction clock, FOSC/4.
feedback.incorrect: Recheck the relationship between FOSC and the instruction clock used by Timer0.

questions.solution: FCY = 4 MHz / 4 = 1 MHz, so one Timer0 increment occurs every 1 us before prescaling.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: Timer0 starts at 0x00, increments every 1 us, and has no prescaler. How many microseconds elapse before the first overflow?

feedback.correct: Correct. An 8-bit timer has 256 states from 0x00 through 0xFF.
feedback.incorrect: Count all 256 Timer0 states. Overflow occurs on the transition from 0xFF to 0x00.

questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes T0IF from T0IE on the PIC16F883?

choices.text: T0IF records the Timer0 overflow event; T0IE controls whether that request is enabled to cause an interrupt.
choices.rationale: The flag and enable have different jobs, matching the interrupt model already used in class.

choices.text: T0IE records the overflow event; T0IF selects the prescaler ratio.
choices.rationale: T0IE is the enable bit and prescaler selection is in OPTION_REG.

choices.text: T0IF selects internal or external Timer0 clocking; T0IE clears TMR0.
choices.rationale: Clock-source selection uses T0CS, and neither bit clears TMR0.

feedback.correct: Correct. Timer0 reuses the event flag versus interrupt-enable model from the interrupt lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Separate the hardware event from the permission gate: T0IF records the request and T0IE controls whether it can cause interrupt service.

questions.solution: T0IF is the Timer0 overflow flag. T0IE is the Timer0 interrupt enable.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter
